clue.text: Letter penned by Charles, so ridiculous

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the run of letters sits inside the words Charles, so ridiculous

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a letter that Charles wrote, calling it ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like a written message, but here it means one who lets property.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who lets out property is literally one who lets, so a letter in that sense is a landlord.

clue.text: Football food with beer and wine

parts.note: pies are the traditional snack sold at British football grounds

explanation.surface: A match-day spread: something to eat at the football, plus beer and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Piesporter is a white wine from the Mosel village of Piesport in Germany.

clue.text: English football team supporter demonstrates how Maradona once performed

parts.note: Man U is the usual short name for Manchester United

explanation.surface: A fan of an English club shows off how the Argentine star Maradona used to play.
explanation.walkthrough: Maradona famously scored with his hand against England in 1986, the 'Hand of God' goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Punching the ball in was done by hand, which is the literal sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Measure of bad experience curtailed, going by public transport?

indicators.note: going by places the shortened word beside the vehicle, after it
curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: a hellish time is a bad experience: hell

explanation.surface: Wondering how bad a trip was after a miserable bus ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' is the definition: an old unit of dry volume, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushel is an old dry volume unit, roughly eight gallons, used for grain.

clue.text: Buddies have this non-British party in British city

indicators.note: in places the party within the letters for British plus city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital city
the ANC, the African National Congress, is a South African political party

explanation.surface: Friends hold a foreign-themed party in a British town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British city' looks like one place, but it is two pieces: a letter, then an Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A close, affectionate friendship between two men is what buddies share, in colloquial use.

clue.text: Notice cut in smart cloth

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word within the other
cut means the final letter is lopped off

explanation.surface: A notice advertises a cut-price sale on smart fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' reads as stylish, but it is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheeting is fabric for making bed linen, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Hanging around in amateur activity creates confusion

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the other

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is amateur home improvement

indicators.note: around signals the word is turned the other way round

parts.note: an arras is a tapestry hanging on a wall

explanation.surface: Someone putting up wallpaper themselves creates a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: An arras is a wall tapestry, named after the French town where such hangings were woven.
explanation.definitionFit: Disarray is a state of disorder or muddle, a near synonym.

clue.text: Trouble with vehicle blocking road? It encourages travel by train

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the middle of, so the pair goes between the letters for road

explanation.surface: A broken-down car blocks the road, so people take the train.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcard gives discounted fares on British trains, so it promotes rail journeys.

clue.text: Time in which to see large round climbing animal loved by kids

indicators.note: in which to see means the reversed bit appears inside the time word

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Over a year, a large round animal is seen climbing, to children's delight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'climbing' means read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon character of Jellystone Park is a famous children's favourite creature.

clue.text: Somehow resolve to ignore very threatening words

indicators.note: somehow suggests the remaining letters are arranged in some other way
to ignore means leaving the letter out

explanation.surface: Firm resolve is undermined by ignoring very threatening words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' drops V from RESOLVE, and 'Somehow' rearranges the remaining RESOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'do it, ___!' is an ultimatum, a phrase that carries a menace.

clue.text: Haughty fool of the upper classes of a ruling dynasty

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
the Ming was a ruling dynasty of China

explanation.surface: A snobbish idiot from a grand family descended from an old dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming in old use means arrogant or presumptuous, a sense close to haughty.

clue.text: Mostly short children being entertained by a clown, following lessons

indicators.note: being entertained by means held inside, as a guest is held by the host
mostly means all but the last letter

explanation.surface: Small children are amused by a clown at a party after school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it describes the children, but it is the word meaning curt.
explanation.definitionFit: Activities held when the school day's classes are over happen after them, hence the adjective.

clue.text: Church sums about to be stashed away for religious events?

indicators.note: stashed away means hidden inside the other letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Church money is about to be hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that rites are not always religious.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal rites such as weddings or baptisms are examples of solemn occasions often held in church.

clue.text: The Old Dominion allows people to wander around

parts.note: the Old Dominion is a nickname for Virginia, abbreviated VA

explanation.surface: Virginia lets people roam freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps and drifters with no settled home roam from place to place.

clue.text: Bumpkin from Scottish island accommodating silly old Penny

indicators.note: accommodating means taking in, holding within

parts.note: Coll is an island of the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: silly signals the letters of the next word are shuffled

explanation.surface: A rustic from a Hebridean island puts up a foolish old woman called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' looks like it describes Penny, but it is the fodder for 'silly'; Penny is just P.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a blockhead or dolt, akin to a country yokel.

clue.text: Man mixed up with a nag uncertain about leaving home

definitions.text: Man mixed up with a nag

indicators.note: about signals the remaining letters are rearranged
leaving signals the home letters depart from the word

explanation.surface: A man tangled up with a horse is unsure about leaving the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops IN from UNCERTAIN, and 'about' rearranges UNCERTA.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical creature is half human, half horse, so a fusion of person and steed.

clue.text: A gala bar opening in summer

indicators.note: bar means except, so the first letter is excluded

explanation.surface: A bar opens for a summer gala.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar opening' removes the F of FESTIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to or occurring during the hot season, as in summertime.

clue.text: Seafarer may have this new hairstyle without fringes

indicators.note: new signals the remaining letters are formed afresh
without fringes means the outer letters at each edge go

explanation.surface: A sailor gets a new haircut with no fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fore-and-aft storm sail is something a sailor's vessel carries.

clue.text: Understand about Russian commune getting stale not working completely

indicators.note: about means going round the commune word

parts.note: a mir was a Russian village commune

explanation.surface: Grasping that a Russian collective farm grew stale and stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has largely quit employment but still does some work is only partly retired.

clue.text: Theme of yarn?

parts.note: a yarn is a story, whose running theme is a line of argument; yarn is also spun fibre, made of strands

explanation.surface: Asking what a story is about.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand of spun fibre, and also the connecting line of a story or argument.

clue.text: See 7
See 8
Drug that is seized by troubled parent

indicators.note: seized by means held inside
troubled signals the letters are disturbed

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A worried parent grabs some medication.
explanation.walkthrough: An aperient is a laxative, a drug in the medical sense rather than a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild laxative medicine, a type of drug that opens the bowels.

clue.text: Female was firm's boss in general

parts.note: to be a firm's boss is to run the company: RAN plus CO, short for company

explanation.surface: A woman was in charge of a company, its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was ... boss' is the past tense: ran.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Franco was the Spanish general who ruled Spain as dictator.

clue.text: Some French seizing ship with silver in a time of barbarity?

indicators.note: seizing means holding within

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Some French pirates seize a silver-laden ship in a lawless era.
explanation.definitionFit: The early medieval period in Europe is popularly seen as an uncivilised era.

clue.text: Sloppy, slightly confused inside, indicating what gives rise to event

definitions.text: indicating what gives rise to event

indicators.note: slightly confused inside means a small shuffle of the inner letters

explanation.surface: A sloppy, somewhat muddled account of why something happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly confused inside' shifts the U of CASUAL one place left.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to cause and effect, describing what brings something about.
